_meta.title: Proverb-a-Day (World English Bible, public domain)
_meta.description: One curated verse from each of the 31 chapters of Proverbs, keyed to the day of the month (day 1 -> chapter 1 ... day 31 -> chapter 31). Ecosystem-generic 864zeros content; not tied to any one app's taxonomy. Each record carries the exact scripture plus an original plain-English rendering.
_meta.translation: WEB (World English Bible), adapted: divine name rendered as 'the Lord'
_meta.license: Public domain (WEB scripture); 'plain' renderings are original 864zeros writing
_meta.source: bible-api.com (WEB); each verse verified verbatim against source, then adapted (see note)
_meta.renderings: text = the WEB scripture (divine name -> 'the Lord'); plain = original 864zeros plain-English 2026 rendering, faithful to the verse's meaning (~grade 6-8), authored not quoted.
_meta.note: Text is WEB (World English Bible); the divine name — WEB's transliteration of the tetragrammaton — has been rendered as 'the Lord' throughout, for cross-app consistency with KJV-style content. Poetic line breaks joined to a single line. Prov 24:16 opens with a capitalized 'For' for standalone presentation (WEB continues the sentence from v.15). No review gate — author is reviewer.

proverbs.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge; but the foolish despise wisdom and instruction.
proverbs.plain: Real knowledge starts with taking God seriously. Only fools brush off wisdom and refuse to be taught.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a reed pen and clay inkwell beside an open manuscript on a reading desk in a well-trod stone footpath diverging at a quiet crossroads

proverbs.text: For the Lord gives wisdom. Out of his mouth comes knowledge and understanding.
proverbs.plain: Wisdom comes from God. Knowledge and understanding come straight from him.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a sower in a simple tunic seen from behind walking a plowed furrow across a quiet stone courtyard shaded by a wide fig tree

proverbs.text: Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and don't lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
proverbs.plain: Trust God with everything you've got — don't rely only on your own take. Bring him into all of it, and he'll keep your path clear.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a narrow footpath bordered by stacked fieldstones winding into a quiet valley in a quiet stone courtyard shaded by a wide fig tree

proverbs.text: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
proverbs.plain: Guard your heart more than anything else, because everything you do flows out of it.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a rough-hewn limestone bench overlooking a quiet valley in a merchant's brass balance scale on a rough wooden table

proverbs.text: For the ways of man are before the Lord's eyes. He examines all his paths.
proverbs.plain: God sees every road you take. Nothing you do is hidden from him.
proverbs.visual_prompt: worn stone steps climbing up a quiet hillside toward an open horizon in a well-trod stone footpath diverging at a quiet crossroads

proverbs.text: Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise;
proverbs.plain: If you're tempted to slack off, watch an ant. Nobody makes her work, yet she just keeps at it. Learn from that.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a rough-hewn limestone bench overlooking a quiet valley in a merchant's brass balance scale on a rough wooden table near a well-trod stone footpath diverging at a quiet crossroads (proverbs 6:6 motif: sluggard)

proverbs.text: Keep my commandments and live! Guard my teaching as the apple of your eye.
proverbs.plain: Live by what's right, and you'll really live. Protect that wisdom like it's the most precious thing you own.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a reed pen and clay inkwell beside an open manuscript on a reading desk in a quiet stone courtyard shaded by a wide fig tree

proverbs.text: For wisdom is better than rubies. All the things that may be desired can't be compared to it.
proverbs.plain: Wisdom is worth more than jewels. Nothing you could want even comes close.
proverbs.visual_prompt: two inscribed stone tablets resting beside an olive branch on a rough ledge in a well-trod stone footpath diverging at a quiet crossroads

proverbs.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. The knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
proverbs.plain: Wisdom begins with taking God seriously. Really knowing him is what understanding is all about.
proverbs.visual_prompt: an unrolled parchment scroll weighted with smooth river stones on a wooden table in a deep stone cistern brimming with clear spring water

proverbs.text: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.
proverbs.plain: Hate keeps fights going. Love covers over the wrongs instead.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a weathered dry-stone boundary wall and wild olive branch in a quiet stone courtyard shaded by a wide fig tree

proverbs.text: When pride comes, then comes shame, but with humility comes wisdom.
proverbs.plain: Pride shows up and shame comes right behind it. Stay humble, and wisdom comes along with it.
proverbs.visual_prompt: an unrolled parchment scroll weighted with smooth river stones on a wooden table in a well-trod stone footpath diverging at a quiet crossroads

proverbs.text: Anxiety in a man's heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
proverbs.plain: Worry weighs a person down, but one kind word can lift them right back up.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a fisherman seen from behind standing on the shore mending a net beside a wooden boat along a well-trod stone footpath diverging at a quiet crossroads

proverbs.text: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when longing is fulfilled, it is a tree of life.
proverbs.plain: Hope that keeps getting put off makes your heart sick — but a longing finally met feels like new life.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a wide-canopied fig tree rooted in rocky soil behind a low dry-stone wall

proverbs.text: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but he who has a quick temper displays folly.
proverbs.plain: Stay calm and you understand a lot. Fly off the handle and you just put your worst on display.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a gnarled fig tree casting open contour lines across rocky ground in a quiet stone courtyard shaded by a wide fig tree

proverbs.text: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
proverbs.plain: A gentle answer cools things down. A harsh word only fires them up.
proverbs.visual_prompt: two inscribed stone tablets resting beside an olive branch on a rough ledge in a well-trod stone footpath diverging at a quiet crossroads near a deep stone cistern brimming with clear spring water (proverbs 15:1 motif: gentle)

proverbs.text: Commit your deeds to the Lord, and your plans shall succeed.
proverbs.plain: Hand your plans over to God, and they'll find their footing.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a rough-hewn limestone bench overlooking a quiet valley in a deep stone cistern brimming with clear spring water

proverbs.text: A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
proverbs.plain: A cheerful heart is good medicine. A crushed spirit drains you dry.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a weathered dry-stone boundary wall and wild olive branch in a well-trod stone footpath diverging at a quiet crossroads

proverbs.text: The Lord's name is a strong tower: the righteous run to him, and are safe.
proverbs.plain: God is like a strong tower — run to him and you're safe.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a massive overhanging crag of weathered limestone sheltering a quiet mountain trail in a quiet stone courtyard shaded by a wide fig tree

proverbs.text: There are many plans in a man's heart, but the Lord's counsel will prevail.
proverbs.plain: You can make all the plans you want, but in the end it's God's purpose that stands.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a weathered dry-stone boundary wall and wild olive branch in a quiet stone courtyard shaded by a wide fig tree near a merchant's brass balance scale on a rough wooden table (proverbs 19:21 motif: many)

proverbs.text: Don't say, "I will pay back evil." Wait for the Lord, and he will save you.
proverbs.plain: Don't tell yourself you'll get even. Wait for God — he'll take care of it.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a gnarled fig tree casting open contour lines across rocky ground in a quiet stone courtyard shaded by a wide fig tree near a merchant's brass balance scale on a rough wooden table (proverbs 20:22 motif: back)

proverbs.text: He who follows after righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness, and honor.
proverbs.plain: Chase after doing right and being kind, and you'll find life, honor, and a clear conscience.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a rough-hewn limestone bench overlooking a quiet valley in a merchant's brass balance scale on a rough wooden table near a well-trod stone footpath diverging at a quiet crossroads (proverbs 21:21 motif: follows)

proverbs.text: A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favor is better than silver and gold.
proverbs.plain: A good name is worth more than being rich. Being respected beats silver and gold.
proverbs.visual_prompt: two robed companions seen strictly from the back walking side by side along a fieldstone trail into a well-trod stone footpath diverging at a quiet crossroads

proverbs.text: Indeed surely there is a future hope, and your hope will not be cut off.
proverbs.plain: There really is a future waiting for you, and your hope won't be cut short.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a weathered dry-stone boundary wall and wild olive branch in a quiet stone courtyard shaded by a wide fig tree near a merchant's brass balance scale on a rough wooden table (proverbs 23:18 motif: indeed)

proverbs.text: For a righteous man falls seven times, and rises up again; but the wicked are overthrown by calamity.
proverbs.plain: Good people fall seven times and get back up every time. Falling isn't the end — staying down is.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a quiet stone courtyard archway opening onto the hills in a merchant's brass balance scale on a rough wooden table

proverbs.text: Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.
proverbs.plain: A person with no self-control is like a city with its walls torn down — wide open to anything.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a mended clay pitcher resting beside a small olive-oil flask on a wooden table in a well-trod stone footpath diverging at a quiet crossroads

proverbs.text: For lack of wood a fire goes out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.
proverbs.plain: A fire dies when the wood runs out. A fight dies when the gossip stops.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a gnarled fig tree casting open contour lines across rocky ground in a quiet stone courtyard shaded by a wide fig tree near a merchant's brass balance scale on a rough wooden table (proverbs 26:20 motif: lack)

proverbs.text: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend's countenance.
proverbs.plain: Iron sharpens iron. In the same way, people sharpen each other.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a dusty desert road winding between scattered boulders toward distant hills in a merchant's brass balance scale on a rough wooden table

proverbs.text: He who conceals his sins doesn't prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.
proverbs.plain: Hide what you've done wrong and you'll stay stuck. Own it and let it go, and you'll find mercy.
proverbs.visual_prompt: an empty clay bowl resting on a rough stone ledge beside a trickling spring in a well-trod stone footpath diverging at a quiet crossroads

proverbs.text: The fear of man proves to be a snare, but whoever puts his trust in the Lord is kept safe.
proverbs.plain: Living for what people think is a trap. Trust God instead, and you're safe.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a stacked fieldstone cairn beside a winding footpath in a quiet stone courtyard shaded by a wide fig tree

proverbs.text: Every word of God is flawless. He is a shield to those who take refuge in him.
proverbs.plain: Every word from God rings true. He's a shield to everyone who takes cover in him.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a massive overhanging crag of weathered limestone sheltering a quiet mountain trail in a quiet stone courtyard shaded by a wide fig tree near a merchant's brass balance scale on a rough wooden table (proverbs 30:5 motif: word)

proverbs.text: Strength and dignity are her clothing. She laughs at the time to come.
proverbs.plain: Strength and dignity are what she wears, and she can laugh at whatever the future holds.
proverbs.visual_prompt: a stacked fieldstone cairn beside a winding footpath in a well-trod stone footpath diverging at a quiet crossroads
